qa.name: Abductor Hallucis
qa.origin: Medial process of the calcaneal tuberosity; flexor retinaculum; plantar aponeurosis
qa.insertion: Medial side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the great toe; medial sesamoid bone
qa.innervation: Medial plantar nerve (L5, S1); abducts great toe — medial border of foot
qa.function: Abducts and assists flexion of the great toe at the MTP joint; supports the medial longitudinal arch
qa.clinical_note: Abductor Hallucis forms the medial border of the foot and is the most medially placed muscle of the first plantar layer. It is the first muscle encountered when approaching the plantar foot medially — a key landmark in tarsal tunnel surgery and plantar fascia release. Weakness or dysfunction contributes to hallux valgus deformity — the great toe drifts laterally as the abductor loses its ability to maintain alignment. The medial plantar nerve (branch of the tibial nerve) innervates the muscles of the medial plantar region.

qa.name: Flexor Digitorum Brevis
qa.origin: Medial process of the calcaneal tuberosity; plantar aponeurosis; intermuscular septa
qa.insertion: Middle phalanges of the lateral four toes — each tendon splits (like FDS in the hand) to allow FDL to pass through
qa.innervation: Medial plantar nerve (L5, S1); flexes lateral four toes — plantar FDS equivalent
qa.function: Flexes the proximal interphalangeal joints of the lateral four toes; assists in gripping the ground
qa.opposing_muscle: Extensor Digitorum Longus and Brevis (toe extension)
qa.clinical_note: Flexor Digitorum Brevis is the plantar equivalent of FDS in the hand — its tendons split to allow FDL (equivalent to FDP) to pass through to the distal phalanges. It lies directly deep to the plantar aponeurosis in the first layer. Plantar fasciitis involves the proximal plantar aponeurosis at its calcaneal attachment — FDB shares this origin and its tightness contributes to the condition. FDB is the central and most prominent muscle of the first plantar layer.

qa.name: Abductor Digiti Minimi
qa.origin: Lateral and medial processes of the calcaneal tuberosity; plantar aponeurosis
qa.insertion: Lateral side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the little toe
qa.innervation: Lateral plantar nerve (S1, S2); abducts little toe — lateral border of foot
qa.function: Abducts the little toe; assists flexion of the little toe MTP joint; supports the lateral longitudinal arch
qa.opposing_muscle: Plantar interossei (adduct toes toward second toe axis)
qa.clinical_note: Abductor Digiti Minimi forms the lateral border of the foot and is the most laterally placed muscle of the first plantar layer. It is innervated by the lateral plantar nerve (unlike Abductor Hallucis and FDB which are medial plantar nerve). Entrapment of the nerve to Abductor Digiti Minimi (a branch of the lateral plantar nerve) as it passes between the deep fascia and the calcaneus is a recognised cause of chronic heel pain — Baxter's nerve entrapment — distinct from plantar fasciitis. Note: also present in the hand as Abductor Digiti Minimi.
